reason: The settled dust and shattered grains may gather into larger solids, but their available partners are not yet clear.
expectation: The inspection should reveal how the pebbles can advance toward a rocky world.

alternatives.reason: Both are disk solids, but their role in forming a world is uncertain.

effect: The pebbles and shattered grains formed a population of rocky bodies through concentration and gravitational collapse.
reaction: The role of gas drag in concentrating the solids was interesting.
reason: Slow encounters between small bodies plausibly allow the new rocky bodies to grow.
expectation: The slowly approaching bodies will gather into a larger rocky world.

effect: Slow accretion produced the young rocky world that will be followed toward a moon-forming impact.
reaction: The connection between gentle growth and the later impact is clear.
reason: The young world and crossing large worlds suggest the impact needed for its moon.
expectation: A collision will transform the young world and produce material relevant to its moon.

effect: The impact heated the growing world into a survivor with a molten interior; a moon has not yet formed.
reaction: The impact changing the existing world rather than replacing it is a useful distinction.
reason: Rubble already orbiting the struck world is the clearest available material for forming its moon.

choice.combine: The rocky world with a molten interior
choice.with: Rubble already orbiting the struck world

expectation: The orbiting rubble will gather into a moon around the surviving world.

effect: The molten world needed metal-rich fragments first; their metal settled to form a dense core.
reaction: I had expected the orbiting rubble to form the moon immediately, so the core-forming step was a surprise.
reason: Now that the world has differentiated, the orbiting rubble remains the clearest candidate for forming its moon.

choice.combine: The rocky world with a dense core
choice.with: Rubble already orbiting the struck world

expectation: The orbiting rubble will gather into a moon around the rocky world.

effect: A second impact created an orbiting debris cloud around the differentiated world; the moon still needs to form.
reaction: I was surprised that another impact was needed before the moon could form.
reason: The struck world now has orbiting impact debris, and the separate orbiting rubble may help it gather into a moon.

choice.combine: The struck world inside an orbiting debris cloud
choice.with: Rubble already orbiting the struck world

expectation: The orbiting material will gather into a moon around the surviving world.

effect: The orbiting rubble gathered with the impact debris to form a moon, completing the first goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the same world retain a moon after both impacts.
reason: Fast rocky projectiles are the clearest candidate for shattering a body, but their target is uncertain.
expectation: The inspection should reveal what the projectiles can strike to begin the remaining goal.

effect: The projectiles shattered a smaller rocky body, creating fragments that can form a rubble body.
reaction: The distinction between the shattered neighbor and the surviving world is clear.
reason: The fragments are the material needed for the remaining goal, but their gathering partner is not yet clear.

choice.inspect: Fragments of a shattered small body

expectation: The inspection should reveal how the fragments can gather into a small world.

effect: The fragments and a slowly approaching body gathered into a rubble world, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the shattered body's pieces form a distinct small world.

mostWorthwhile.text: Forming a moon around the same world after its impacts was worthwhile because it brought its history together.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying orbiting rubble twice before the world was ready felt repetitive, although the feedback advanced the sequence each time.

surprise.text: The world needed a core-forming step and then another impact before its moon could form.

arbitrary.text: The need to add metal-rich fragments before the moon-forming impact was not obvious to me from the available pieces.

continue.text: I would continue: following the same world's transformations and the contrasting fate of its shattered neighbor made me curious about what happens next.
